title: Large language models
stage: Graduate study and research in machine learning
audience: a graduate preparing for research in machine learning, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD or a research role
purpose: Understand large language models from the inside: the transformer language model in detail, tokenization, pretraining data and objectives, scaling laws and compute-optimal training, emergent abilities and the debate about them, fine-tuning and instruction tuning, learning from human feedback and preference optimization, in-context learning and prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, tool use and agents, efficient inference, evaluation and benchmark contamination, and open problems such as hallucination.
primary_reading: Stanford CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch (free lectures and assignments)

weeks.1: The transformer language model in detail
weeks.5: Emergent abilities and the debate about them
weeks.7: Learning from human feedback: reward models and RLHF
weeks.8: Preference optimization without reinforcement learning: DPO and related methods
weeks.9: In-context learning, prompting and retrieval-augmented generation
weeks.11: Efficient inference: caching, quantization and decoding
weeks.12: Evaluation, contamination, hallucination and open problems

blocks.deliverable: Count the parameters of a transformer from its configuration.
Use a scaling law to choose a model size for a compute budget.
Explain how the choice of metric can make an ability look sudden.
Week 7 midterm; compute a reward-model loss on preference pairs.
Design and evaluate a retrieval step for a question-answering system.
Design an evaluation for a capability and check it for contamination.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Small language model study: train a small character- or word-level transformer language model on a supplied public-domain text with any framework on your own computer, measure loss against model size or data size and fit a simple scaling curve, implement two decoding methods, and write a short paper with your measurements, sample outputs and a discussion of what the results do and do not show about larger models.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
